The design conversation settled most of cert-tags. Drafting the spec left two choices it never ruled on — both change what an owner sees or what data is kept, so they're yours. Everything else (limits, field types, error codes) I'll record as assumed and list at the end.

**Q1 — What deleting a tag does**

When an owner deletes a tag, what happens to the certificates that carry it?

**Why it matters:** this decides whether a delete can silently lose information an owner put on many certificates, and whether a delete can fail.
**What it affects:** the `CertificateTag` join rows in `api`, the tag manager in `web` and `mobile`, and the confirm dialog both consumers show.
**Recommendation:** remove the tag from every certificate, after a confirm that names how many carry it — it's how the existing "delete owner group" flow behaves (`apps/web/src/features/owners/DeleteGroupDialog.tsx:22`), and it never leaves an owner stuck on a delete they can't finish.

turns.question: When an owner deletes a tag, what happens to the certificates that carry it?

options.label: Untag everywhere (Recommended)
options.description: Delete removes the tag from every certificate after a confirm showing the count. Simple, matches the owner-group delete; the tagging is gone for good.

options.label: Block while in use
options.description: Delete is refused until no certificate carries the tag. Nothing is lost by accident, but the owner must untag each certificate first.

options.label: Archive instead
options.description: The tag is hidden from pickers and filters but stays on certificates. Nothing is lost; adds an archived state and a way to restore it.

turns.text: Untag everywhere

**Q2 — Who sees a certificate's tags**

Should a certificate's tags be visible to everyone who can see the certificate, or only to its owner?

**Why it matters:** tags are free text owners type; showing them to other viewers makes a private note public.
**What it affects:** the `tags` field on `GET /certificates` and `GET /certificates/:id` in `api`, the chips on the list in `web` and `mobile`, and the read-only owner view.
**Recommendation:** owner only — the owner view already hides `notes` from non-owners (`apps/api/src/routes/certificates.ts:61`), and tags are the same kind of owner-authored text.

turns.question: Who should see a certificate's tags?

options.label: Owner only (Recommended)
options.description: Tags are returned only to the certificate's owner; other viewers see no chips and can't filter by them. Matches how notes are treated today.

options.label: Everyone who can see it
options.description: Tags show to every viewer of the certificate, and they can filter by them. Tags become shared labels — owners must not put private text in them.

turns.text: Owner only
Never 'Right / Change something' — each question is a real decision with its alternatives. Under --auto each takes its recommendation, recorded auto (recommended) YYYY-MM-DD.

Written and committed as `docs(ACME-412): design cert-tags`. Here's what cert-tags will do — 3 parts, one at a time.

**Part 1 of 3 — What users get**

**What changes for users**
- Before: an owner finds "everything for the site B audit" by scrolling the certificate list.
- After: an owner tags certificates with their own labels ("audit 2026", "site B") and filters the list by one or more tags — on the web and in the mobile app.
- Who: certificate owners. Other viewers see nothing new — tags are private to the owner.

**What they'll see**
- Certificate list (web, mobile) — chips under each name, a Tags filter beside Status:
```
┌ Certificates ─────────────────── [Status ▾] [Tags ▾] ┐
│ Boiler 3 — gas safety                  due 12 Nov    │
│   (audit 2026) (site B)                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
- Owner view — a Tags row with *+ Add tag*; typing offers the tags you already have.
- Settings → Tags — rename, recolour, delete. Delete asks first: *"Remove 'site B' from 14 certificates?"*

**Added · Changed · Removed**
- Added: tags on certificates · the Tags filter · Settings → Tags · tag endpoints in api
- Changed: the certificate list takes an optional tag filter
- Removed: nothing

The review is the design approval (REFERENCE §The review): plain words and the product's own names — screens, buttons, fields — never §-shorthand, and no file to open. Too long for one screen, so it comes in parts, one per turn, each ending in A/B.

**Part 2 of 3 — Data and apps**

**Data**
- New: a tag (name, colour, owner) and a link between tags and certificates.
- Existing: certificates are untouched — every one starts with no tags.
- Migration: one, additive — two new tables, nothing altered; undone by dropping them.
- Deleting a tag deletes its links only; the certificates are never touched.

**Apps**
- **api** — stores tags, returns them to the owner only, filters the list. Built first.
- **web** — the chips, the filter, the owner-view editor, Settings → Tags.
- **mobile** — the same chips, filter and editor. Released app: people on today's version see no change and nothing breaks — every field it reads stays as it is.

**Part 3 of 3 — Decisions and risks**

**Decisions**
- Deleting a tag takes it off every certificate, after a confirm naming the count — not blocking the delete while in use (owners stuck untagging one by one).
- Only the certificate's owner sees its tags — not every viewer (private notes made public).
- A tag name is 1–32 characters, unique per owner ignoring case *(assumed)*
- Up to 200 tags per owner, 20 per certificate *(assumed)*
- Adding a tag name you already have reuses that tag *(assumed)*
- Colours come from the 8 chip colours already in use — no free colour picker *(assumed)*

**Risks and open questions**
- Filtering a long list by several tags could be slow — an index on the link is planned; the audit checks the query.
- Nothing open.

**Not included**
- Tags shared between owners or across a team.
- Tagging many certificates at once.
- Tags in exports and reports.

**What the audit changed in the design you approved**
- **What they'll see** — + *"No certificates match these tags"* when a tag filter matches nothing, on web and mobile (nothing said what an empty result shows).

- **Decisions** — two new, for you: several tags — match all or any; mobile — edit tags or only filter. Both carry a recommendation.

**What the pass found**

**Data integrity — first**
- Deleting a tag must remove its `CertificateTag` rows in the same transaction; the spec said "untag everywhere" but no cascade was written. Fixed: `onDelete: Cascade` on the join, §Schema row SC3.
- Ownership: `PATCH /certificates/:id` has no owner check (`apps/api/src/routes/certificates.ts:88`). Per your call it's fixed in the api phase, and the new tag endpoints get the same guard (T4).

**Released build (mobile)**
- `tags` on `GET /certificates` is a new optional field — additive, safe for mobile 3.2 in the store, which ignores unknown keys (`apps/mobile/src/api/certificates.ts:14`). Stated in §Apps *Backward compatibility*.

**Contract-changing**
- The list filter was `?tag=<id>`; web's existing filter bar sends repeated params (`?status=a&status=b`). §Contract now reads `?tag=<id>` repeatable on `GET /certificates`. The scoped second pass checked this one row against both consumers: clean.

- No empty state was specified for "no certificates match these tags" on either consumer — written into §web and §mobile, reusing `EmptyState`.

**Stale spec**
- The web filter component is `ListFilters` (`apps/web/src/features/certificates/ListFilters.tsx`), not `CertificateListFilter`. Fixed in place.

**Nits** — two field names aligned to the API's camelCase transform.

**Build-time risk** (not a blocker): mobile's offline list cache keys on the query string, so a stale tag filter may show after a tag is deleted — settled by the mobile filter task.

**Open decisions (2)** — multi-tag filtering ALL vs ANY; whether mobile can edit tags or only filter. Both carry a recommendation.
